title: One blast and all fall. Another, and all stand.
subtitle: The Horn that ends and begins

row.title: the Horn
sub: all in heavens and earth fall

then: Ibn Kathir says after the blast all life ends, until only the Ever-Living remains and asks: {idea}whose is the kingdom this day?{/idea} Then the Horn is blown again and {idea}they stand, looking on.{/idea}
now: Your alarm goes off and you are up in seconds, half asleep, standing before you know it. {idea}That is how fast the second call will be.{/idea} Wake up today in a way you would like to wake up then.
old: The Day of Resurrection feels far off and unreal.
new: One call will raise everyone at once, and I will be standing among them.
try: When your alarm rings tomorrow, remember the second blast and say alhamdulillah as you rise.

title: The earth lit by its Lord's light, and the Book laid open.
subtitle: The court of the Day sets up
then: Ibn Kathir says the earth will shine when Allah comes {idea}to pass judgement.{/idea} Qatadah said the Book is the record of deeds. Ibn Abbas said the prophets will bear witness against their nations. {idea}No one will be wronged.{/idea}
now: You have watched a court case online where the evidence was missing and the guilty walked. It stung. {idea}On that Day nothing is missing and no one is wronged.{/idea} That is comfort and a warning in one.
old: Justice in this world often fails, so maybe it always does.
new: On that Day every record is laid out and judgment is in complete truth.
try: Do one thing today you would be glad to see in your own record.

title: Every soul paid in full for what it did.
subtitle: He knows best what they do
then: The verse closes the scene of judgment: {idea}every soul paid in full{/idea}, and Allah knows best what they did. Nothing depends on witnesses alone.
now: You stayed late to help a colleague and your manager never found out. You lost your temper with the cashier and no one you know saw. {idea}Both are counted, in full.{/idea}
old: If no one sees it, it does not really count.
new: Every deed, seen or unseen, is paid in full by the One who knows best.
try: Do one quiet good deed today that no one will thank you for.

title: Did no messengers come to you? Yes, they did.
subtitle: The question at the gate
then: Ibn Kathir says the keepers ask whether messengers came {idea}of your own kind, so you could have spoken to them and learned.{/idea} They answer: yes. {trap}They came and warned us, and we rejected them.{/trap}
now: Your doctor warned you. Your friend warned you. The verse you read warned you. You can picture having to say: yes, I was told. {idea}Let the answer be: yes, and I listened.{/idea}
old: Nobody ever really made the truth clear to me.
new: The warnings have reached me; what matters is whether I listen.
try: Think of one warning you have been given about your conduct, and act on it today.

title: A wretched home for the arrogant.
subtitle: Where pride leads
then: Ibn Kathir says the words are not given a speaker, as if {idea}all creation testifies they deserve it.{/idea} He names the cause: {trap}arrogance in this world and refusal to follow the truth.{/trap}
now: You notice it in small ways: refusing to say sorry first, dismissing advice from someone younger, never asking for help. {idea}Pride starts small.{/idea} So can humility.
old: A bit of pride is just self-respect.
new: Arrogance that refuses truth is what leads to the worst end.
try: Say sorry first in one disagreement today, even if you think you are partly right.

title: Peace be upon you. You have done well. Enter.
subtitle: The welcome at the open gates
then: Ibn Kathir says they go in groups, each with its peers, after injustices between them are settled. The gatekeepers meet them {reward}with greetings of peace and praise.{/reward} What follows is not mentioned, {idea}left for the heart to hope.{/idea}
now: You remember arriving home after a long trip and someone at the door saying welcome back. That warmth. {reward}Now imagine angels saying: peace be upon you, you did well.{/reward}
old: Paradise is too abstract for me to feel anything about.
new: It begins with a personal welcome: peace, you did well, come in.
try: Greet the people at home with salam today, warmly, the way you hope to be greeted.

title: Praise to Allah, who kept His promise to us.
subtitle: The first words inside
then: Inside the gates, the first words are praise. {idea}He fulfilled His promise.{/idea} They settle wherever they wish, and call it {reward}an excellent reward for those who worked.{/reward}
now: The years of waking for Fajr in winter. The money you gave when it was tight. The tongue you held. It felt like no one saw. {reward}One day you will say: He kept His promise.{/reward}
old: My small efforts for Allah probably do not add up to much.
new: Every effort is part of a promise Allah will keep in full.
try: Say alhamdulillah for one hard act of worship you kept up this year.

title: It all ends with praise to the Lord of the worlds.
subtitle: The last word of the surah
then: Ibn Kathir says the praise has no named speaker, so {idea}all of creation praises Allah for His wisdom and justice.{/idea} Qatadah said Allah began creation with praise and {reward}ended it with praise.{/reward}
now: You end most days with a scroll and a sigh. Try ending it the way creation will end: {reward}alhamdulillahi rabbil alamin.{/reward} The day was judged fairly too.
old: My day ends when I run out of energy.
new: Everything ends in praise of Allah, and my day can too.
try: Before you sleep tonight, say alhamdulillahi rabbil alamin and mean it for the whole day.
